content.title: Louisville Kings vs Orlando Storm score highlights, UFL schedule
content.text: April 4, 2026Updated April 5, 2026, 1:00 a.m. ETThe Louisville Kings were in Orlando, Florida, for their first road game as a member of the UFL.The Louisville Kings are 0-2 after losing to the Orlando Storm (2-0).Coverage from the game:Louisville Kings drop UFL road game to Jack Plummer, Orlando StormCoverage during the game:The Louisville Kings had a near-perfect United Football League debut last week in front of an announced crowd of 14,034 at Lynn Family Stadium.Everything but the final score: 15-13, Birmingham Stallions."If these people had fun today, we're going to give them a lot better shows in the future," coach Chris Redman said after the loss. "That was not our best at all."The Kings (0-1) will try to earn their first win on the road today against the Orlando Storm (1-0) at Inter&Co Stadium.The Storm beat the Columbus Aviators in Week 1, 23-16. They're led by former UofL quarterback Jack Plummer under center. He threw for 245 yards and a touchdown in his UFL debut last week.Here's everything you need to know to follow today's game from home, including live score updates:FINAL | Orlando 19, Louisville 9The Kings fall to 0-2, while the Storm improve to 2-0.Click here to read our instant takeaways from the game.2:31, 4Q | Louisville's Deantre Prince picks off Orlando's Jack PlummerPlummer and the Storm were looking to add to their fourth-quarter lead, but Deantre Prince had other plans: picking off the former Cardinals QB in the end zone.4:59, 4Q | Orlando 19, Louisville 9The Storm might have just put this one on ice with a 39-yard touchdown pass from Plummer to Elijhah Badger.0:00, 3Q | Orlando 12, Louisville 9Nothing doing for either team during the third quarter.The Kings punted twice and had a turnover on downs at the Storm's 41-yard line during the period.Same for the Storm: two three and outs and a turnover on downs around midfield.10:37, 3Q | Orlando 12, Louisville 9Both the Storm and the Kings punted after three and outs on their opening drives of the second half.Redman went with starting quarterback Jason Bean on Louisville's first drive out of the locker room after his backup, Chandler Rogers, completed nine of his 13 pass attempts for 116 yards before the break.HALF | Orlando 12, Louisville 9Switching to Chandler Rogers at quarterback after the first two drives of the night has paid off for Redman. The Kings enter the locker room with 174 total yards — 92 less than what they had at the end of last week's loss.And yet ... they still can't get the ball into the end zone. In the first quarter, Rogers missed a read and left a receiver wide open for what would have been an easy touchdown. In the second, two false start penalties scattered across four snaps pushed the offense back from Orlando's 18-yard line to the 24 — facing a third down and 16.The defense bent but didn't break ... until giving up that 41-yard touchdown from Plummer to KJ Hamler with 24 seconds to spare before the intermission. The Storm will receive the opening kickoff of the second half.0:24, 2Q | Orlando 12, Louisville 9Disaster moments before halftime for the Kings' defense, which had the Storm facing a third down and 19 but allowed Plummer to connect with KJ Hamler for a 41-yard touchdown.Orlando's extra-point attempt was no good.2:00, 2Q | Louisville 9, Orlando 6The longest drive in Kings history, 73 yards in 11 plays, ends in a 32-yard field goal from Tanner Brown.Chandler Rogers quarterbacked the drive, which featured a 22-yard catch and run from Benny Snell Jr. you'll see below:Rogers is 9 for 13 with 116 yards through the air so far tonight. He also came up with this 12-yard scramble during the scoring drive:8:49, 2Q | Louisville 6, Orlando 6We're tied up again after an 11-play, 53-yard Storm drive ends in another field goal from Michael Lantz.Nice red-zone stand from the Kings defense. Orlando got as far as Louisville's 5-yard line, but the visitors delivered a tackle for loss (-3 yards) on second down. The Storm didn't gain another yard after that.12:55, 2Q | Louisville 6, Orlando 3Redman went with Chandler Rogers under center for the Kings' latest drive, and the California grad led the team 65 yards in 10 plays to the Storm's 23-yard line.Louisville had to settle for another field goal from Tanner Brown, this one from 41 yards out, after Rogers missed a wide-open Tarik Black in the end zone on a backside read on third and 7.5:05, 1Q | Louisville 3, Orlando 3The Storm answer with a field goal of their own. This one was a 57-yarder from Michael Lantz.7:38, 1Q | Louisville 3, Orlando 0Tanner Brown gets the Kings on the board with a 42-yard field goal.The biggest moment of the five-play, 28-yard drive: Jason Bean connecting with tight end Tre' McKitty for a 21-yard gain on Play 1.9:43, 1Q | Louisville 0, Orlando 0We're scoreless after an opening drive from both the Kings and the Storm. Louisville just forced a turnover on downs at its 47-yard line.The Kings mustered nine yards in three plays before punting to end their first drive of the night.Louisville Kings vs Orlando Storm starting on ESPNewsToday's game between the Kings and the Storm will begin on ESPNews. You'll also be able to stream it via ESPN.com and the ESPN app.Louisville Kings vs Orlando Storm start timeThe Kings and the Storm are set for an 8:05 p.m. kickoff today at Inter&Co Stadium.Louisville Kings vs Orlando Storm oddsSpread: Storm -3½ points (-110)Over/under: 40½ points (-110)Money line: Orlando -185, Louisville +150Note: Odds via BetMGM.What channel is Louisville Kings vs Orlando Storm on today?Today's game between the Kings and the Storm will air on ESPN, which is channel 602 on AT&T U-Verse; channel 206 on DirecTV; channel 140 on Dish; and channel 506 on Spectrum.If you subscribe to a cable package, you'll be able to livestream the game via ESPN.com and the ESPN app. If you don't have cable, you can livestream the game via Fubo, which offers a free trial here.
